tooling: any OpenAI-compatible client; curl against POST {base}/chat/completions
chaining: pairs with a lightweight interactive caller; the one-reply-per-30-seconds-per-IP floor is the scarce link and it is shared with every other caller on the address

limits.value: 1 reply every 30 seconds per IP on the anonymous tier
limits.source: 402 body: 'Free limit reached: 1 reply every 30 seconds per IP'

free_tier.stated: the Classic API lists one model, openai-fast, described as 'GPT-OSS 20B Reasoning LLM (OVH)', with aliases openai, gpt-oss, gpt-oss-20b and ovh-reasoning
free_tier.notes: the served model is OVH-hosted gpt-oss-20b, so this endpoint is a relay of the OVH public tier rather than a separate allocation

identity_cost.detail: no key required, but the allowance is metered per IP and shared with everything else on that address

reliability_note: the same model on the same base URL returned 402 and 404 an hour apart, and 404 and 402 in reverse order's two runs
confidence_note: the per-IP 402 was observed. The advertised id openai-fast is listed by GET /models with the aliases openai, gpt-oss, gpt-oss-20b and ovh-reasoning, and a completion for openai-fast reports the served model as gpt-oss-20b, so the served model is the advertised one under one of its aliases.

records.tps_basis: streamed chars/4 / (time_total - time_starttransfer) on a second, streaming call, run 1 only

probe.timing_note: latency_ms and ttft_ms on a row came from two different requests in the original instrument, which is how five rows ended up with ttft_ms > latency_ms. They are corrected here from a re-probe on 2026-10-22T04:38:22Z with probe3.py, which takes both fields from one streaming request: 475 ms total and 475 ms to first byte. The earlier run-1 figures (3501 ms latency, 2532 ms ttft) are kept because both came from one request pair that was internally consistent.

evidence.proved: requesting openai-fast returned 200 with model gpt-oss-20b echoed, a substitution; 51 completion tokens in the written run, and re-probed at 2026-10-22T04:38:22Z at 475 ms total with 475 ms to first byte on one streaming request. The recon run's 289 ms figure is withdrawn: its ttft_ms on the same row was 499 ms, so the two fields describe two different calls and neither can be quoted as a latency
requesting gpt-5-nano returned 402 'Free limit reached: 1 reply every 30 seconds per IP' in run 1 and 404 'isn't on the Classic API' in run 2, eight minutes apart

evidence.proved: one POST with no Authorization header for openai-fast answered 200 with content NEEDLE-9K2X; body model gpt-oss-20b and user_tier anonymous; headers x-model-used: gpt-oss-20b, x-usage-prompt-text-tokens: 324, x-usage-completion-text-tokens: 51, x-usage-total-tokens: 375; no rate-limit header (Retry-After is exposed only on a refusal)
GET /models lists one model, openai-fast, described as GPT-OSS 20B Reasoning LLM (OVH), tier anonymous, with aliases openai, gpt-oss, gpt-oss-20b and ovh-reasoning

notes: openai-fast is an alias for gpt-oss-20b served from OVH, so this endpoint duplicates docs/inference/free's OVH row under a different name and a tighter limit. The 402 is the finding: a keyless endpoint exhausted by per-IP budget with no account in existence.
